title: Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - National
subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: When a local US government uses federal grant money to fund a procurement, they must comply with a sweeping set of federal administrative requirements, cost principles, and audit rules. What is the common citation for this uniform guidance?
options: The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)
UCC Article 2
2 CFR 200 (Uniform Guidance)
Title IX
questions.explain: 2 CFR 200 (Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards) is the definitive set of rules—commonly known as the Uniform Guidance—that non-federal entities must follow when spending federal grant funds.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Under 2 CFR 200, public agencies using federal funds are explicitly required to take 'all necessary affirmative steps' to ensure that they use which types of businesses when possible?
options: Fortune 500 corporations
International conglomerates
Minority businesses, women's business enterprises, and labor surplus area firms
Local vendors located strictly within city limits
questions.explain: 2 CFR 200.321 strictly mandates that non-federal entities must take six affirmative steps to assure that minority businesses, women's business enterprises, and labor surplus area firms are used when possible.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A local agency is applying geographical preferences (giving bonus points to hometown vendors) on an RFP. Suddenly, the project receives a massive federal grant making it fully federally funded. According to 2 CFR 200, what must the agency do regarding geographical preference?
options: Increase the preference points to support local federal taxpayers.
Remove the geographic preference, as 2 CFR 200 explicitly prohibits the use of statutorily or administratively imposed state or local geographical preferences in the evaluation of bids or proposals.
Request a waiver from the local Mayor to keep the preference.
Change the geographic preference to encompass the entire state rather than just the city.
questions.explain: 2 CFR 200.319(c) explicitly states that the non-Federal entity must conduct procurements in a manner that prohibits the use of statutory or administratively imposed state, local, or tribal geographical preferences in the evaluation of bids or proposals, except where applicable Federal statutes expressly mandate or encourage geographic preference.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Under the Build America, Buy America Act (BABA) guidelines linked to federal infrastructure funding, a public agency constructing a water treatment plant must ensure that all of the iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials used in the project are:
options: Produced in the United States
Produced within the state where the project occurs
Procured using low-bid methodologies only
Exempt from the Uniform Commercial Code
questions.explain: The Build America, Buy America Act (BABA) implements strong domestic content procurement preferences, requiring that all iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials used in federally funded infrastructure projects be produced in the USA.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Under the federal Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200), if a local government executes a purchase below the 'Micro-purchase Threshold' using federal funds, they may:
options: Award the contract without soliciting competitive quotations, provided they consider the price to be reasonable.
Publish a formal RFP for 30 days.
Bypass checking SAM.gov for vendor debarment entirely for all future purchases.
Only buy from minority-owned businesses.
questions.explain: Micro-purchases under 2 CFR 200 allow an agency to acquire supplies or services without soliciting competitive price or rate quotations if the non-Federal entity considers the price to be reasonable based on research, experience, or recent purchases.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: When preparing a solicitation that will be funded by federal grants, what type of contract is expressly disfavored or heavily restricted under 2 CFR 200?
options: Firm Fixed-Price Contracts
Time and Materials (T&M) Contracts
Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contracts
Requirements Contracts
questions.explain: Under 2 CFR 200, a Time and Materials (T&M) contract is heavily restricted and may only be used after a determination that no other contract is suitable, and if the contract includes a ceiling price that the contractor exceeds at its own risk.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: When purchasing specialized equipment under a federal grant (2 CFR 200), a sole-source (non-competitive) procurement is permitted ONLY if:
options: The buyer really likes the vendor's previous work.

The item is available from only one source, there is a public exigency/emergency, the federal awarding agency expressly authorizes it, or after solicitation of a number of sources, competition is determined inadequate.
The purchase exceeds $100,000.
The agency has a longstanding geographic preference for the vendor.
questions.explain: 2 CFR 200.320 dictates strict rules for noncompetitive procurement. It can only be used under specific circumstances: true sole source availability, emergency/exigency, explicit approval by the federal awarding agency, or inadequate competition after a good faith effort.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: To comply with the 'Byrd Anti-Lobbying Amendment' linked to federal grants, contractors who bid for an award exceeding $100,000 must file a certification stating:
options: They have not paid and will not pay anyone using appropriated federal funds to influence an officer or employee of any agency or Congress regarding the award.
They will hire at least three federal lobbyists to manage the grant.
They will limit all profit margins to 5%.
They have never donated to a political campaign.
questions.explain: The Byrd Anti-Lobbying Amendment prohibits the use of federal funds to pay persons or organizations for influencing or attempting to influence the executive or legislative branch with respect to obtaining a federal contract or grant. Bidders must certify compliance.
